display.purpose: Page headings. One per view, always in the header. Serif texture is the brand signal.

headline.purpose: Card titles, section headings within pages. Carries authority without display scale.

body.purpose: All readable text. Inter's OpenType alternates are active for optimized letterforms.

label.purpose: Section labels, field labels, metadata categories. Wide tracking and uppercase are the hierarchy signal.

mono.purpose: Model names, DOIs, search term chips, note editing. Gives data a distinct texture.

shadows.name: drawer

motion.name: ease-opacity

narrative.overview:
A well-lit surface in a dim room. Papers spread flat, annotations visible, tools within reach. LitFolio's interface is a reading desk, not a dashboard: the content (papers, highlights, evidence) occupies the foreground, and the chrome recedes into near-darkness. Density is deliberate; every pixel serves the researcher's flow of import, read, ask, and retain.

This system rejects the patterns PRODUCT.md names explicitly: generic chatbot shells where output disappears into scrolling transcripts, dashboard-heavy SaaS styling that prioritizes decoration over reading, and magic-looking AI flows that hide source provenance. It also rejects the visual cliches of its category: no neon-on-black 'AI tool' aesthetic, no white-space-heavy 'productivity app' template. The reference benchmark is Linear: dense, keyboard-driven, minimal chrome, information-first with precise spacing.

Glassmorphism is used deliberately on elevated surfaces (drawers, overlays, floating panels) to maintain the layered desk metaphor. Main content surfaces use tonal depth (paper, panel, ink) rather than blur.
keyCharacteristics: Content-forward: the reading surface dominates; navigation and controls are narrow and quiet
Tonal depth through three background layers (ink, paper, panel), not through shadows
Violet accent used sparingly for state and emphasis, never for decoration
Functional transitions only; no entrance choreography or decorative motion
Dense typography with strong serif/sans contrast for hierarchy

rules.name: The Rarity Rule
rules.body: The violet accent is the only color that signals interactivity. Its rarity is the point. If every other element is violet, the system has failed.

rules.name: The Tinted Neutral Rule
rules.body: No pure black (#000) or pure white (#fff) anywhere. Every neutral leans toward the plum undertone of the body gradient.

rules.name: The Serif Anchor Rule
rules.body: Every page has exactly one serif heading at text-2xl in the header. If a view has no serif heading, it has no visual anchor; add one.

rules.name: The Label Case Rule
rules.body: Section labels and field labels are always uppercase with 0.05em tracking. Never sentence case, never bold. The transform itself is the hierarchy signal.

rules.name: The Three-Layer Rule
rules.body: Every surface maps to ink, paper, or panel. If you need a fourth depth, you're over-nesting. Flatten.

rules.name: The Blur Boundary Rule
rules.body: Backdrop blur belongs to overlays and floating surfaces only. Main content never uses blur.

rules.name: The One Accent Button Rule
rules.body: Each view has at most one Primary button visible at a time. If two primary actions compete, one must be downgraded to Secondary.

rules.name: The Dense Row Rule
rules.body: List rows use px-6 py-3.5 padding. They are tighter than cards because they are content, not containers.

dos: Use the three-layer tonal system (ink, paper, panel) for all depth decisions
Keep the violet accent to interactive elements and active states only
Use serif (Lora) for exactly one heading per page view, at text-2xl with tight tracking
Use text-[11px] uppercase tracking-wider for all section labels and field labels
Use backdrop blur on overlays and floating surfaces only
Use transition-colors duration-150 on all interactive state changes
Use Muted Ink (#6b6b78) for all secondary text, metadata, and timestamps
Use Signal Amber for dirty/unsaved state and Signal Emerald for saved state
donts: Use generic chatbot shells where output disappears into a scrolling transcript
Use dashboard-heavy SaaS styling that prioritizes decoration over reading and evidence
Use magic-looking AI flows that hide source provenance or silently degrade on failure
Use pure black (#000) or pure white (#fff)
Use side-stripe borders (colored border-left > 1px) on cards, list items, or callouts
Use identical card grids with icon + heading + text repeated endlessly
Use modals as the first solution
Use bounce or elastic easing curves
Apply backdrop blur to main content areas
Use more than one Primary button per visible view
Use the violet accent for decoration, backgrounds, or large surfaces
